applies_why: The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on a link clash, which is exactly what this rule governs.
quote: the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.
room: 'never a ground': one reading is that the judge's lead clause makes Matthew 1:16's admitting both readings itself the reason the clash cannot be decided; the other is that the clause is mere context and the verdict rests on weighing the two chains; I weighed the first, because the stated ground after the dash is the single verse's dual admission, and the cited rounds are recorded only as who answered what, with no comparison of chain support.
why: The judge made the fact that one verse (Matthew 1:16) admits both readings the stated ground for UNDERDETERMINED, which K-S2 says can never be a ground.
